claim.statement: Current AWS security documentation says Kiro can read, create, modify, search and delete files and run filesystem-impacting commands in both Autopilot and Supervised modes, while protected paths require explicit approval.

source.title: Kiro privacy and security
source.locator: Autopilot versus supervised mode and Protected paths

limitations: This is a publisher description, not an observed permission-enforcement receipt for 1.0.288.
unknowns: Workspace, target paths, operation mode, command policy and approval results are unknown.

claim.statement: Current AWS documentation distinguishes Autopilot, where changes can be applied without per-step approval, from Supervised, where Kiro yields after a turn containing file edits for hunk or file review; both retain interrupt and revert paths.

source.title: Kiro Autopilot
source.locator: How it works and change management features

limitations: Supervised review follows tool writes to disk and is not evidence that no pre-review filesystem mutation occurs.
unknowns: The effective mode, pending changes, checkpoints and review decisions are unknown.

claim.statement: Current Kiro terminal documentation says commands require approval by default, can be run once or added to a prefix-based trusted list, and can be forced back to manual review by a substring-based command denylist.

limitations: Prefix trust applies to an entire command string and does not establish semantic analysis of chains, pipes or redirects.
unknowns: Trusted and denied patterns, proposed commands, modifications, approvals and outputs are unknown.

claim.statement: Current Kiro MCP documentation says configured servers can expose tools, Kiro can select them, tools request approval by default, named tools may be auto-approved, and servers or individual tools may be disabled.

source.title: Kiro MCP tools
source.locator: Managing individual tools and Tool approval process

limitations: MCP servers are external components with their own authority and are not identified by the Kiro client version.
unknowns: Servers, transport, tools, schemas, parameters, credentials, disabled lists and approvals are unknown.

claim.statement: Current Kiro model documentation says a user can select a named model and supported effort level or use Auto for publisher-controlled per-task routing, with availability varying by region.

lifecycle.reason: Rolling model inventory and service routing.

limitations: A model label or Auto choice does not identify provider endpoint, weights, service revision or fallback behavior.

claim.statement: Current Kiro documentation says Quick Spec generates requirements, design and task artifacts without approval gates between phases, while standard Feature Specs retain review gates before implementation.

limitations: This claim concerns planning artifacts and phase gates; it does not establish approval of later file changes or commands.
unknowns: Spec type, artifact contents, review decisions, task selection and implementation state are unknown.

claim.statement: Current Kiro hook documentation says configured events can trigger either an agent prompt or a local shell command, and that pre-tool or prompt-submit command failures can block the associated invocation.
